S052-01.notes: 'Hedging nearly every conclusion and noting the limits' = cautious/circumspect, contrasted with later confidence. 'Speculative' is the main trap (it suggests tentativeness but means conjectural, the opposite of hedging). Perfunctory and derivative have no textual support. Vocabulary level of 'circumspect' pushes it toward medium.

S052-02.notes: The hypothesis is that kinship words come from early infant sounds, so father words should also use early sounds (papa/baba/dada: bilabials and dentals are early babble sounds, consistent with Jakobson-style accounts). A over-applies the specific m sound; if father words also began with m, the words would not distinguish parents. B and C contradict or replace the hypothesis. Factually sound.

S052-03.notes: Text presents the tradeoff view, cites studies challenging it, then cautions that the findings do not extend to large increases. B overstates ('never'), C covers only the first sentence, D has no recommendation. Characterization of minimum-wage research (e.g., Card-Krueger line, Cengiz et al.) is accurate and appropriately hedged.

S052-04.notes: Claim has two parts: steady decline in X and nonconsistent decline in Y. Only C shows X's monotonic drop and Y's rise-then-fall. D is the trap: true but shows only endpoints, so it cannot establish steadiness or inconsistency. B covers Y only and endpoints only; A is irrelevant. Data in C match the table.

S052-05.notes: Two independent clauses ('The city's archive had been closed...for decades' / 'researchers were finally admitted in 2019') joined by a coordinating conjunction need a comma + but. A lacks the comma (run-on by SAT convention), B is a comma splice, C puts a semicolon before 'but', which is nonstandard. Inserted D reads cleanly.

S052-06.notes: 'By the time the rescue team reached' (past) + duration 'for nearly six hours' before that past point requires past perfect progressive; parallel 'were showing' confirms past frame. B and C are present-frame; D is future.

S052-07.notes: The sentence concedes evidence for the critics' charge (two-page chapter, unresolved subplots) before the 'Yet' rebuttal, the classic concession structure for 'Admittedly'. Thus wrongly makes the short chapter a consequence of the critics' judgment; Similarly and Instead do not fit. Trap: some will pick Thus because the second sentence elaborates the first.

S052-08.notes: Only B generalizes, drawing on all three examples plus the taxonomic note. A and D are single examples; C omits tool use. Facts check out: sea otters use rocks as anvils/hammers for shellfish; New Caledonian crows make hooked tools from twigs and pandanus leaves; veined octopuses carry and assemble coconut shell halves as shelters (Finn et al. 2009). 'Food or shelter' is accurate.
